talks.title: Arming WinRAR: Deep dive into clusters of SideCopy APT and its correlation with Transparent Tribe
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in Arming WinRAR: Deep dive into clusters of SideCopy APT and its correlation with Transparent Tribe.
talks.summary:
Overview: Satyajit of Quick Heal presents at Botconf on SideCopy APT's evolution from HTA-based stages to MSI-based attacks, with correlations to parent group APT36 and Transparent Tribe.

Key Topics: SideCopy targeting government officials and university students; transition from HTA to MSI delivery mechanisms; multi-platform attack capabilities; infrastructure correlation with APT36; and WinRAR exploitation in recent campaigns.

Technical Details: The research traces SideCopy from HTA-based mshta execution through archive files containing shortcut triggers, to MSI-based stages targeting Indian government and education sectors. Correlation analysis links infrastructure to APT36 operations.

Takeaways: SideCopy demonstrates how regional APT groups evolve delivery mechanisms while maintaining operational infrastructure. Defenders in South Asia should monitor for both HTA and MSI-based initial access patterns.

talks.title: Stronger Together - Disrupting The Ngioweb Botnet Powering The NSOCKS Proxy Service
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for Stronger Together - Disrupting The Ngioweb Botnet Powering The NSOCKS Proxy Service.
talks.summary:
Lumen Visibility and No-Route Disruption

Chris from Lumen Black Lotus Labs describes disrupting the NGO web botnet powering malicious proxy services. As a major ISP, Lumen observes global peering traffic and can “no-route” malicious servers so traffic never reaches them—scaling botnet takedowns beyond single-victim cleanup.

Residential Proxy Abuse Model

Malicious proxy services pose as legitimate offerings while recruiting infected residential hosts via IoT exploitation, cracked software bundles, and free VPN apps. Unlike benign providers with clear consent, these networks rotate compromised IPs cheaply for anonymity, blurring lines between gray-market proxies and outright botnets.

Collaborative Takedown

The talk covers NGO web malware architecture and industry collaboration to disrupt operations, then examines post-disruption effects on the proxy marketplace. Infection vectors and unstable proxy lifetimes illustrate why defenders must treat cheap residential proxies as potential crimeware infrastructure.

talks.title: Tricky obfuscation techniques for C2 communication ? Just detect them all !
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of Tricky obfuscation techniques for C2 communication ? Just detect them all !.
talks.summary:
Network Detection Stack

A malware analyst with five-plus years in traffic threat hunting outlines a pyramid from reputation lists through signatures, sandboxing, and advanced fuzzy-hash or ML analysis. Each layer trades freshness for generality; IOC lists rot quickly while ML adds false positives.

Detection Methods in Practice

Signature rules (e.g., Emerging Threats loaders matching plaintext system-info beacon fields) break when attackers tweak content. Open rule sets from Positive Technologies and others supplement ET, though some community packs stagnate. Sandboxes like ANY.RUN help interpret ambiguous bytes in PCAPs.

C2 Obfuscation Focus

The core session covers popular C2 hiding techniques that complicate network analysis—embedded in HTTP/TLS/DNS patterns—and demonstrates how layered analytics (not IOCs alone) can still surface malicious sessions. The speaker shares research via social platforms showing live traffic examples.

Takeaway for Analysts

Effective C2 defense combines reputation, signatures, sandbox confirmation, fuzzy clustering, and ML features—no single tier suffices as attackers rotate infrastructure and encode payloads dynamically.

talks.title: Threat Intelligence On Steroids: Exploits, Ransomware And Other Threats At Scale
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of Threat Intelligence On Steroids: Exploits, Ransomware And Other Threats At Scale.
talks.summary:
Motivation

SentinelOne threat intelligence engineer Sart Mishra (notDucky) explains that most tooling detects what malware does—registry keys, dropped files—not how it does it. Packers, TTP tweaks, and obfuscation break static rules; actors rarely rewrite entire codebases.

Harbinger project

Over six to seven months he built Harbinger, a side-project automation suite for large-scale trend analysis and attribution. He forked CAPE Sandbox to extend unpacking heuristics, change artifact streaming, and avoid relying on in-VM agent RPC behavior he disliked.

Rule engine

Harbinger exposes a C interface for low-level behavioral rules—example: detecting failed device-handle allocation during bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver scenarios. It maintains separate hunting and attribution rule sets, treats packed and unpacked memory similarly, and clusters behavior to MITRE techniques.

Goal

By focusing on implementation patterns rather than surface indicators, defenders can track evolution across ransomware, exploits, and other threats more resiliently than VirusTotal-style impact queries alone.
